new_statements.quote: Les langues sous étude ont deux tons simples et deux tons complexes. Nous choisissons de ne pas noter les tons bas, mais seulement les tons haut ´, montants ˇ ou descendants ˆ.
new_statements.translation: The languages under study have two simple tones and two complex tones. We choose not to mark low tones, but only high ´, rising ˇ or falling ˆ tones.

new_statements.rule_in_words: ɛnyá is a tone language with lexical H/L tone plus rising and falling contours; the source says nothing about word stress or accent placement. No opened source makes any statement about stress in Enya; the only full phonology (Spa 1973, 'Traits et tons en enya') is print-only and, per its reviewer, treats tone rules.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement applies jointly to ɛnyá, mokpá and metóko as transcribed in the authors' 2019-2021 fieldwork wordlists (lexical items, citation forms). Tone only; no stress domain is discussed.
new_statements.identity_note: All opened sources concern the same language: Spa 1973/1975 describe the enya of the baenya/wagenya fishers at Kisangani (Houis 1975: ~7,000 speakers, Guthrie D14) = enya1247; Kopa wa Kopa & Ricquier 2023 use ɛnyá data collected south of Kisangani along the lower Lualaba (2019-2021), ISO gey, ~15,000 speakers = enya1247. Bukungu Batangana 1981 ('kigenya', written at ISP Kindu) may instead concern the Kindu-area Enya/Songola variety (Glottolog Enya-Kindu, no ISO code; the earlier scan's enya1249), so it should not be assumed to describe enya1247 without checking.

sources.locator: footnote 7, p. 8 (section on the corpus and notation)
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. Footnote 7 (p. 8): the three languages (ɛnyá, mokpá, metóko) have two simple and two complex tones; low tones left unmarked, high ´, rising ˇ, falling ˆ marked. Data from Kopa wa Kopa's own fieldwork south of Kisangani 2019-2021; notes that Spa 1973 is the only real phonology of ɛnyá and that a detailed phonological study of the three languages remains to be done.
